learning_outcomes.text: Handling methods, techniques and tools for project design, organization, and management.
Skill in handling information and communication systems in the industrial field.
Skills for generating project documents and other similar technical documents.
Skill in the technical management of projects in the field of industrial engineering.
Skills for adequately communicating documents, procedures, and results in the field of Industrial Engineering.

syllabus_topics: Presentation of the Teaching Guide, work methodology, work groups, information and communication sources, and computer knowledge and applications for the course.
Introduction to the Technical Office, functions, work organization, teamwork techniques, integration with company systems, decision making, communication.

Industrial project concept, classification, structure and life cycle. Project documents: index, report, drawings, specifications, budget and studies with their own entity. Standardization. UNE 157002. Project report: structure and content.
Project drawings structure and index. Representation typology: dimension and relationship. Title block. Sizes and scales. Folding. Criteria for drawing preparation.
Legislative framework and interpretation of technical legislation applied to the specialty: municipal regulations, occupational risk prevention and Technical Building Code.
Basic concepts of fire protection: fire, typology, fire prevention systems. Application of fire prevention regulations in industrial establishments.
Basic construction elements: roof, foundation, structural elements, coatings, carpentry and finishes. Examples.
Installation design methodology: types of installations. Determination of loads. Elements for supplying loads. Actuation, control and safety elements. Installation drawings and schematic diagrams.
Budget and planning: measurement and economic valuation. Project management and planning theory. Methodology for preparing a plan: project breakdown structure, databases and plan elaboration.
Specification types: administrative, technical and facultative. Project bidding and contracting.
Studies with their own entity: studies related to compliance with occupational risk legislation: basic safety and health study. Studies related to compliance with waste management legislation.
Other technical documents: concept of technical report, classification and structure. Certifications. Homologations, appraisals and valuations.

Professional activity: processing (visa, notary, public bodies, etc.); management of licenses, authorizations and permits before public institutions and private entities; project bidding and contracting.
Industrial property: technological innovation and industrial property. Patents and utility models.
Communication: techniques for oral and written presentation of work.
assessment_rules: The default evaluation system is continuous assessment, which requires attendance and participation in at least 80% of practical classes. To pass continuous assessment, a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required for each assessable activity and a final minimum of 5 out of 10 as a weighted average. Students who opt for global evaluation or fail continuous assessment must take a single exam consisting of 40% theoretical content, 40% practical content, and 20% communication skills, requiring a minimum of 5 out of 10 in each block and overall. Any fraudulent conduct, such as copying or plagiarism, will result in a final grade of 0.0 for the academic year.
